primary_benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, ankles, thighs and groins, abdomen and chest, and throat, and deep hip flexors (psoas)
Strengthens the back muscles
Improves posture
Stimulates the organs of the abdomen and neck
instructions: From a prone position with the abdomen on the earth, the hands grip the ankles (but not the tops of the feet) with knees no wider than the width of your hips
The heels are lifted away from the buttocks and at the same time the thighs are lifted away from the earth working opposing forces as the heart center, hips and back open
The gaze is forward
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Dhanurasana draws the whole front body open like a strung bow, generating strong heat. It is powerfully Kapha-reducing and kindles Agni through direct abdominal compression. Pitta types should hold it briefly and avoid it in peak summer; Vata types need a warm spine first, as a cold deep backbend is where the lumbar complains.

primary_benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, the ankles, thighs and groins, abdomen and chest, and throat
Stretches the deep hip flexors (psoas)
Strengthens back muscles
Improves posture
Stimulates the organs of the abdomen and neck
instructions: From a kneeling position the knees are hip width apart and the thighs are perpendicular to the earth
The inner thighs are narrowed and rotated slightly inward with the buttocks engaged but not hardened
The tailbone is tucked under but the hips do not puff forward
The shins and tops of the feet are pressed firmly into the earth
The ribcage is open, along with the heart center, but the lower front ribs do not protrude sharply towards the sky
The lower back lifts the ribs away from the pelvis to keep the lower spine as long as possible
The base of the palms are pressed firmly against the soles (or heels) of the feet and the fingers are pointed toward the toes
The arms are extended straight and are turned slightly outward at the shoulder joint so the elbow creases face forward without squeezing the shoulder blades together
The neck is in a relatively neutral position, neither flexed nor extended, or (for the advanced practitioners only) the head drops back
Be careful not to strain your neck and harden your throat
The gaze is either towards the sky or towards the earth, depending upon your flexibility
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Ustrasana opens the heart centre and the throat, releasing the emotional holding that settles in the chest. The strong extension is heating and Kapha-clearing, and the throat opening stimulates the thyroid. Because it can provoke a rush of emotion or dizziness, Vata types should keep the hands on the sacrum rather than reaching for the heels.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the erector spinae and mid-back extensors that stabilise posture
Opens the chest and intercostals, increasing usable lung capacity
Stimulates the abdominal organs and supports digestive motility
Counteracts the thoracic rounding built up by desk and phone posture
instructions: Lie prone with the legs together, tops of the feet pressing down, and the forehead resting on the mat.
Place the palms flat beside the lowest ribs, elbows bent and hugging close to the side body.
Inhale and peel the chest away from the floor by contracting the back muscles — take almost no weight into the hands.
Draw the shoulder blades down the back and widen across the collarbones; keep the elbows soft and pointing back, never splayed out.
Press the pubic bone toward the mat to lengthen the lumbar spine rather than compressing it.
Gaze forward and slightly down. Exhale to lower with control, one vertebra at a time.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lift the chest, exhale to lower. Never hold the breath at the top.
ayurvedic_rationale: Bhujangasana opens the chest — the seat of Prana Vayu and Sadhaka Pitta — lifting the heaviness and low mood that accumulate with excess Kapha. The gentle abdominal compression kindles Agni. Pitta types should keep the pose light and stop well short of maximum depth, as forceful backbending adds heat.

primary_benefits: Removes fatigue
Improves breathing and the circulation of blood to the brain
Rejuvenates the entire body
instructions: From  box neutral the ribcage is lifted with a gentle sway in the low back
The tailbone lifts up into dog tilt
The eyes are soft and the gaze is to the sky
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Bitilasana is the extension half of the Cat-Cow pair — the gentlest spinal backbend available. The breath-linked movement grounds Vata, the mild pace keeps Pitta from rushing, and the mobilisation lifts the morning stagnation of Kapha. It is the safest possible warming of the spine for every constitution.

primary_benefits: Opens the chest, throat, and shoulders
Encourages thoracic extension and postural counterbalance
May ease mild tension from rounded shoulders and forward head posture
Supports deeper breathing by expanding the rib cage
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs extended or bent as comfortable.
Slide your hands under your hips with palms down, or keep the arms alongside the body if needed.
Press the forearms and elbows into the floor and lift the chest by arching the upper back.
Gently rest the crown of the head on the floor only if the neck remains comfortable and uncompressed.
Keep the throat soft and the chest open while breathing evenly.
To come out, lower the head and torso slowly and release the hands from beneath the hips.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to broaden the chest and rib cage, and exhale slowly to soften the throat and upper back.
ayurvedic_rationale: Matsyasana is traditionally used to open the heart and throat channels, encouraging freer prana flow through the upper body. The chest-expanding shape can be uplifting for kapha while the gentle backbend helps relieve stiffness and dryness associated with vata.

primary_benefits: Deeply stretches the quadriceps and hip flexors
Opens the chest and front line of the body
Strengthens the back muscles and glutes
Improves spinal extension and mobility
instructions: Lie on your stomach with the forehead on the mat.
Bend one knee and reach back to hold the foot or ankle, then repeat on the other side.
If accessible, draw the heels gently toward the outer hips while keeping the knees comfortable.
Lift the chest slightly and press the pubic bone down to protect the low back.
Keep the shoulders broad and the breath steady as you hold the shape.
Avoid forcing the knees or lower back; reduce the depth if there is strain.
Release slowly by lowering the chest and extending the legs back to the floor.
pranayama_sync: Use slow, even breaths and exhale to soften the thighs and chest without forcing the backbend.
ayurvedic_rationale: This strong opening posture can stimulate sluggish Kapha while building heat and vitality. Because it is intense and expansive, it is best used with care to avoid aggravating Vata in sensitive joints or the lower back.

primary_benefits: Opens the entire front line — hip flexors, abdomen, chest, throat
Builds deep thoracic and lumbar spinal extension
Strengthens the back body and shoulder girdle under load
Stimulates the thyroid and parathyroid through sustained throat extension
instructions: Begin kneeling with the thighs vertical and the shins parallel, hip-width apart.
Place the palms on the sacrum, fingers pointing down, and draw the elbows toward one another.
Inhale and lift the sternum toward the ceiling, arching the upper back first while the hips stay stacked over the knees.
Slowly release the head back only if the neck is entirely comfortable, then walk the hands down to reach for the feet.
In the full expression the forearms rest on the floor and the crown approaches the soles of the feet.
Come out the way you came in, leading with the chest, then rest in Child's Pose for at least as long as you held the pose.
pranayama_sync: Steady Ujjayi throughout. If the breath becomes ragged, come out immediately.
ayurvedic_rationale: Kapotasana is among the most demanding backbends and generates intense Pitta. It suits robust Kapha constitutions with an established practice and should be approached with restraint by Pitta types, particularly in Grishma (summer). Vata types need thorough warming first, as cold, unprepared joints are where injury happens.

primary_benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and quads
If the elbow is used to push the thigh, it opens the hips as well
instructions: Lie on the back in supine position
Bend the knees, heels close to SI bones and cross one ankle over the opposite knee
Thread the hands or reach through between the thighs
Lift the foot off the floor and hold the bent knee behind the thigh or shin to bring it closer to the chest, make sure that the acrum is rooted to the floor
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Supta Kapotasana opens the deep external rotators and the psoas, releasing the pelvic region governed by Apana Vayu. The hips hold the residue of unprocessed stress, which is why this pose so often surfaces emotion. Long, supported holds are deeply Vata-pacifying; forcing depth is Vata-aggravating.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the spine and back extensors
Opens the chest and shoulders
Improves posture and counteracts slumping
Gently energizes the body and supports respiratory expansion
instructions: Lie on your stomach with the legs extended and the tops of the feet on the floor.
Place the hands beside the ribs or alongside the body depending on comfort.
Inhale and lift the chest slightly off the mat, using the back muscles more than the hands.
Keep the neck long and gaze slightly forward or down to avoid compressing the neck.
Draw the shoulder blades gently together and down the back.
Hold the posture with smooth breathing and moderate effort.
Exhale to lower the chest back to the floor with control.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lift the chest and create space through the front body, then exhale to maintain steady support in the back.
ayurvedic_rationale: This mild backbend stimulates circulation and awakens the spine, making it useful for reducing Kapha heaviness and supporting Agni. Its moderate, grounding effort can also steady Vata when performed without strain.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the spine
Stretches the chest, the lungs, the shoulders and the abdomen
Stimulates the abdominal organs
Opens the heart and the lungs
instructions: From a prone position with the pelvic bowl is firmly contracted interiorly towards the center line of the body while the pubis is tucked under
The legs are extended back and the tops of the feet are flat
The palms are flat and the elbows are on the mat, stacked right below the shoulders
On an inhalation, lift the sternum and extend the neck away from shoulders with the elbows, palms and pelvic bone firmly attached to the mat
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Salamba Bhujangasana is the most accessible backbend in the system — the forearm support means the lower back is never asked to hold the weight. It gently stimulates the adrenals and kidneys and opens the chest without heat, making it the backbend of choice where Cobra is contraindicated and the safest extension for a Vata-disturbed lumbar spine.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the back, glutes, and core
Improves balance and coordination through opposite-limb engagement
Stretches the front of the thigh and hip
Encourages spinal mobility and body awareness
instructions: Start on hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Extend one leg straight back and lift it to hip height or as comfortable.
At the same time, reach the opposite arm forward or keep both hands grounded for stability.
Keep the pelvis level and the core engaged to protect the low back.
Lengthen through the spine and avoid collapsing into the shoulders.
Breathe steadily as you hold, then lower with control.
Repeat on the other side after a brief rest.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen the lifted arm and leg, and exhale to stabilize the core and lower back.
ayurvedic_rationale: Tiger Pose builds heat, circulation, and coordinated strength, which can help reduce Kapha sluggishness and support healthy movement. The rhythmic cross-body action also helps organize Vata when practiced with steady breath and control.

primary_benefits: Strengthens wrists, arms, shoulders, and posterior chain
Opens the chest and front body
Improves hip extension and spinal mobility
Can counteract slumping from prolonged sitting
instructions: Sit with your legs extended straight in front of you and place your hands on the floor slightly behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet.
Press firmly through the palms and heels, then lift the hips until the body forms a long diagonal line.
Keep the chest broad and the shoulder blades drawing gently down the back.
Engage the thighs and glutes to keep the pelvis lifted and stable.
Maintain a neutral neck by either looking forward or slightly upward without compressing the throat.
Breathe steadily while holding the pose, then lower the hips with control on an exhale.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lift and expand the chest, and exhale to maintain steady core engagement and controlled support.
ayurvedic_rationale: This pose builds heat and strength while opening the chest and anterior body, which can help reduce heaviness and lethargy associated with kapha. Its uplifting quality also supports vata by grounding through the legs and stabilizing the shoulders.

primary_benefits: Improves posture
Strengthens the spine, arms, and wrists
Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, and abdomen
Firms the buttocks
Stimulates abdominal organs
Helps relieve mild depression, fatigue, and sciatica
Therapeutic for asthma
instructions: The body is in a prone position parallel to the earth
The weight of the body is supported equally by the straight arms and the tops of the feet which press firmly into the earth
The shoulders are rotated back and down
The ribcage is lifted and pulled thru to the front in a slight upper thoracic backbend
The joints are stacked with the wrists, elbows and shoulders in a straight-line
The neck is a natural extension of the spine and the chin is slightly tucked
The abdomen is pulled up towards the spine
The palms are flat and the elbows are close to the side body
The gaze is forward
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Urdhva Mukha Svanasana lifts the whole body off the floor on the hands and the tops of the feet, making it far more demanding than Cobra. The strong chest opening awakens Prana Vayu and clears Kapha heaviness. The thighs must stay lifted — dragging them along the mat dumps the entire load into the lumbar spine.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, legs, buttocks, abs, and spine
Stimulates the thyroid and pituitary
Increases energy and counteracts depression
Therapeutic for asthma, back pain, infertility, and osteoporosis
instructions: Pressed up from a supine position, lying on your back, the palms are rooted into the earth with the fingers pointed towards the heels
The feet are grounded
The hips are pressed up
The thighs are rotated inward
The thoracic spine is arched creating a strong crescent arch along the spinal column
The gaze is forward
pranayama_sync: Inhale as you open the chest, exhale to deepen
ayurvedic_rationale: Urdhva Dhanurasana is the full expression of spinal extension and generates intense heat throughout the system. Strongly Kapha-reducing and energising, but markedly Pitta-provoking — it should be practised in the cool of the morning rather than in Grishma heat. Requires thorough preparation of the shoulders and thoracic spine.

primary_benefits: Opens the chest, shoulders, and side body
Builds balance and coordinated full-body strength
Encourages spinal extension and hip opening
Can feel uplifting and energizing
instructions: Begin from a side plank or three-legged downward-facing dog transition.
Root firmly through the supporting hand and outer foot.
Open the chest toward the sky while lifting the free arm overhead or behind you.
Keep the lifted hip elevated and avoid collapsing into the supporting shoulder.
Engage the core and legs to maintain balance and protect the low back.
Breathe evenly, then return slowly to the starting position with control.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lift the chest and open the side body, and exhale to ground through the supporting hand and foot.
ayurvedic_rationale: This expressive backbend can enliven stagnant Kapha and support a sense of lightness and openness. Because it is stimulating and unstable, it may increase Pitta and should be practiced with moderation and clear alignment.

primary_benefits: Builds balance and full-body coordination
Strengthens the standing leg and core
Opens the hips and hamstrings
Improves concentration and body awareness
instructions: Begin in a bound side-angle or bound half-bound shape with a stable base.
Shift weight into the standing foot and engage the standing leg strongly.
Slowly lift the back leg off the floor while maintaining the bind and torso stability.
Begin to rise, extending the lifted leg as you come upright if balance allows.
Keep the chest open and the gaze steady at one point ahead.
Breathe evenly, using the exhale to stabilize and the inhale to lengthen.
To exit, bend the lifted knee, lower the leg with control, and release the bind carefully.
pranayama_sync: Keep the breath slow and even, using each exhale to steady the standing leg and each inhale to create length through the spine.
ayurvedic_rationale: This pose is energizing and expansive, useful for mobilizing kapha while building focused, disciplined steadiness. Because it requires strong containment and concentration, it can help channel scattered vata into clear, directed effort.

primary_benefits: Strengthens arms and wrists
Stretches the upper back
Strengthens the abdominal muscles
Opens the groin
Tones the abdominal organs
instructions: From an inverted position, with the hips up and the head down, the arms are bent in a 90-degree angle with the knees resting on the elbows
The palms are firmly rooted into the earth with knuckles pressed firmly into the earth for support
The belly is pulled up and in towards the spine with the ribcage and chin lifted
The weight of the body shifts slightly forward as the toes lift up and off the earth into the full expression of the pose
The gaze is down and slightly forward
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Bakasana is the gateway arm balance, and the obstacle it addresses is mental more than physical. The forward commitment over the hands cultivates the fearlessness and focus of a steady Pitta mind, while the effort clears Kapha inertia. Vata types gain real grounding from bearing their own weight, once the wrists are conditioned.

primary_benefits: Develops single-leg balance and proprioceptive control
Opens the front of the shoulder, chest, and hip flexor of the lifted leg
Strengthens the standing ankle, calf, and gluteal complex
Trains sustained concentration through drishti
instructions: Stand in Tadasana and shift the weight into the right foot, grounding evenly through all four corners.
Bend the left knee and catch the inside of the left ankle with the left hand, thumb pointing up.
Extend the right arm forward and up, and fix your drishti on a still point at eye level.
Press the left foot firmly back into the hand — the pressing, not the pulling, is what lifts you.
Hinge the torso forward as the left thigh lifts behind you, keeping the hips level and the standing leg straight but not locked.
Hold, then release the foot slowly and return to Tadasana before changing sides.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen and lift, exhale to steady. Keep the breath even — balance follows breath.
ayurvedic_rationale: Natarajasana demands the steadiness (sthira) that scattered Vata most needs, while the backbend and single-point gaze lift Kapha's inertia. The pose is named for Shiva as lord of the cosmic dance — it asks for poise inside movement rather than rigidity.

primary_benefits: Strengthens and stretches the ankles and calves
Stretches the thighs, hips, shoulders, and upper back
Improves concentration
Improves sense of balance
instructions: From a standing position the one thigh is crossed over the other with the toes and/or the ankle hooked behind the lower calf
The weight of the body is balanced on the standing foot
The arms are crossed in front of the torso so that one arm is crossed above the other arm
The top arm is tucked into the elbow crook of the bottom arm
The hands are hooked around each other as well
Once hooked, the elbows lift up and the fingers stretch towards the ceiling
The gaze is soft and forward
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Garudasana wraps the limbs inward, compressing the joints and then flooding them with circulation on release. The bound, contained shape is markedly Vata-pacifying — it gathers scattered energy toward the midline — while the single-leg balance demands the concentration that quiets a busy mind.

primary_benefits: Builds significant arm, wrist, and shoulder strength
Develops deep core and oblique control under load
Opens the hips and hamstrings in a compressed position
Trains the fear-management and focus that arm balances demand
instructions: From a seated position, hook the right knee over the right shoulder as high onto the upper arm as it will go.
Plant both palms on the floor, shoulder-width apart, fingers spread wide and pointing forward.
Cross the left ankle over the right and squeeze the legs firmly together — the grip of the ankles holds the pose.
Press down through the hands, lift the hips, and shift the weight forward until the feet leave the ground.
Bend the elbows to 90 degrees as in Chaturanga and extend the legs out to the right side, torso lowering toward parallel.
Gaze forward. To exit, straighten the arms, lower the hips, and unwind the legs.
pranayama_sync: Exhale to lift and shift forward. Keep breathing — holding the breath collapses the pose.
ayurvedic_rationale: Astavakrasana generates strong Pitta — heat, effort, and determination. It is well suited to Kapha constitutions needing activation, and should be practised sparingly by Pitta types prone to pushing past their limit. Vata practitioners benefit from the grounding of bearing their own weight, but only once the wrists and shoulders are genuinely conditioned.

primary_benefits: Opens the hips and groins
Stretches the hamstrings, IT bands and legs
Improves balance
instructions: From mountain
html pose, lift one foot
Bend forward and catch the toes with the fingers
Place the other hand on the hip to square the hip towards the front
Slowly straighten the knee and the torso and open the leg to one side
Use a strap if necessary
Gaze towards the front or opposite of the extended leg for balance
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana demands hamstring length and single-point focus at the same time, exposing any wobble in either. The steadiness it asks for is precisely what scattered Vata needs. Use a strap around the foot rather than rounding the spine to reach — the compromise in the spine is never worth the reach.

primary_benefits: Builds arm, wrist, and shoulder strength
Deeply stretches the hamstrings, inner thighs, and adductors
Strengthens the hip flexors and deep core
Improves overall body awareness and balance on the hands
instructions: Stand with the feet slightly wider than hip-width and fold forward, walking the hands behind the heels.
Bend the knees deeply and work the shoulders as far under the backs of the thighs as possible.
Plant the palms flat behind the feet, fingers pointing forward, and grip the floor.
Shift the weight back into the hands and lift the feet off the floor, resting the thighs high on the upper arms.
Straighten the legs out to the sides as much as the hamstrings allow, pointing through the toes.
Lift the chest and gaze forward. Lower with control by bending the knees and setting the feet down.
pranayama_sync: Exhale to lift off. Maintain a steady Ujjayi throughout the hold.
ayurvedic_rationale: Tittibhasana requires both heat and precision, making it a Pitta-dominant practice. Kapha types gain from the vigour and lightness it cultivates. Vata practitioners should warm the hamstrings and hips thoroughly first, as forcing this pose cold risks strain at the adductor insertion.

primary_benefits: Builds substantial upper-body and core strength
Opens the hamstrings and hip flexors simultaneously
Develops the balance and commitment required for arm balances
Strengthens the wrists and the serratus and pectoral stabilisers
instructions: Begin in a low lunge with the right foot forward, then thread the right shoulder under the right thigh.
Plant both palms shoulder-width apart on the floor, fingers spread and pointing forward.
Bend the elbows to a Chaturanga angle, creating a firm shelf for the right thigh on the right upper arm.
Shift the weight forward over the hands until the back foot lifts off the floor.
Extend the right leg straight forward and the left leg straight back, forming a split in the air.
Gaze forward. Lower the back foot first, then release the front leg, and repeat on the second side.
pranayama_sync: Exhale to shift forward and lift. Breathe steadily; the pose collapses on a held breath.
ayurvedic_rationale: Eka Pada Koundinyasana is intensely Pitta-generating — it rewards precision and courage but punishes forcing. Best suited to Kapha constitutions that benefit from activation, and to seasoned Pitta practitioners willing to work without competition.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the abdomen, ankles, thighs, buttocks and spine
Stretches the groins, hamstrings, calves, shoulders, chest and spine
Improves coordination and sense of balance
Helps relieve stress
Improves digestion
instructions: From a standing position one leg is straight while the other is extended back parallel to the earth (or a little above parallel) and one hand is on the earth (beyond the little-toe side of the foot, about 12 inches) while the other hand is extended up towards the sky
The shoulder blades are squeezed together and the fingers move outward in opposing directions
The weight of the body is supported mostly by the standing leg while the bottom hand has very little weight on it but is used intelligently to regulate balance
The upper torso is rotated open to the sky
Both hips are externally rotated
Energy is extended actively through the flexed toes to keep the raised leg strong
The inner ankle of the standing foot is lifted strongly upward, as if drawing energy from the earth
The sacrum and scapulae are firmly pressed against the back torso and lengthen the coccyx toward the raised foot
The gaze is either up or down, depending on the condition of the neck
If injured the gaze is down
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Ardha Chandrasana opens the whole side body while balancing on one leg and one hand — expansion and stability held together. The lunar name signals its cooling, receptive quality, making it well suited to Pitta. A block under the bottom hand is standard practice, not a beginner's concession.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, and spine
Tones the abdomen
instructions: The body is parallel to the earth
The weight of the body is supported by straight arms and active toes
The abdomen is pulled up towards the spine and the pelvis is tucked in
The neck is a natural extension of the spine and the chin is slightly tucked
The palms are flat and the elbows are close to the side body
The joints are stacked with the wrists, elbows and shoulders in a straight line perpendicular to the earth
The gaze follows the spine and the eyes are focused down
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Phalakasana builds the core stability that protects the spine — the primary seat of Vata — in every other posture. The sustained isometric effort generates heat and strongly reduces Kapha. Pitta types should watch the tendency to grit through it; the pose ends when the lower back starts to sag, not when willpower runs out.

primary_benefits: Improves balance and coordination
Strengthens the standing leg and core
Mobilizes the thoracic spine with rotation
Stretches the hamstrings and hips
instructions: Start in a standing balance setup, often from a lunge or half moon variation with one hand on the floor or a block.
Shift weight into the standing leg and lift the back leg until the body is stable.
Place the opposite hand to the floor or block and begin rotating the torso toward the standing-side leg.
Stack the hips as much as possible while keeping the lifted leg active and extended.
Reach the upper arm upward or keep it on the hip if balance is challenging.
Maintain a long spine and steady gaze slightly forward or downward.
Exit slowly by returning the lifted leg to the floor and unwinding the torso with control.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen through the crown and lifted heel, and exhale to rotate and stabilize without holding the breath.
ayurvedic_rationale: This twisting balance stimulates circulation and clear directional energy, making it useful for reducing kapha stagnation and supporting mental focus. The pose can also refine vata by training steadiness, though it should be approached with calm, measured effort.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, and shoulder girdle
Builds oblique and deep core strength through the twist
Improves spinal rotation and detoxifying abdominal compression
Develops balance, focus, and confidence on the hands
instructions: Begin in a deep squat with the feet and knees together, heels lifted.
Twist the torso to the right, bringing the left elbow to the outside of the right thigh.
Plant both palms on the floor to the right, shoulder-width apart, fingers spread and pointing away from you.
Bend both elbows to 90 degrees, keeping them stacked directly over the wrists and hugging in toward the midline.
Rest the outer right thigh on the left upper arm, then shift the weight forward and lift the feet.
Keep the knees together and gaze past the fingertips. Lower with control and repeat on the second side.
pranayama_sync: Exhale to deepen the twist and shift forward. Never hold the breath in a loaded twist.
ayurvedic_rationale: The twist compresses and then flushes the abdominal organs, kindling Agni and helping clear Ama. The heat and effort are Pitta in nature and strongly reduce Kapha. Vata types should approach slowly with a warm spine, as cold rotation under load is where the lumbar complains.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the wrists, shoulders, and obliques
Improves core stability and lateral body strength
Builds balance and proprioception
Helps develop full-body integration and endurance
instructions: Begin in Plank Pose with shoulders stacked over wrists and legs active.
Shift weight into one hand and roll onto the outer edge of the same foot.
Stack the other foot on top or place it slightly in front for stability.
Lift the free arm toward the ceiling or keep the hand on the hip for support.
Engage the abdomen and lift the hips so the body forms a straight line.
Keep the neck long and gaze steady, then breathe evenly before switching sides.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen through the crown and exhale to lift the hips and engage the core, keeping the breath steady and unforced.
ayurvedic_rationale: This pose generates heat and stability while strengthening the side body and core, which can help counter kapha heaviness and vata instability. Because it is effortful and energizing, it is best practiced with steady breath and moderation if pitta is elevated.

primary_benefits: Improves balance and concentration
Strengthens the standing leg and feet
Builds hip stability
Promotes calm focus and body awareness
instructions: Stand tall with your feet together or hip-width apart.
Shift weight into one foot and ground down through all four corners of that foot.
Place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or inner thigh, avoiding the knee joint.
Bring your hands to prayer at the heart or reach them overhead.
Keep the standing hip steady and gently draw the ribs in to support balance.
Fix your gaze on one point and breathe evenly.
Release the lifted foot slowly and repeat on the other side.
pranayama_sync: Use slow, even breaths to steady the gaze and maintain balance without gripping.
ayurvedic_rationale: Tree Pose is grounding and centering, making it especially supportive for scattered vata and restless mind states. By building steadiness through the legs and focus through the breath, it also helps mobilize kapha in a balanced way.

primary_benefits: Strengthens the ankles and legs
Strengthens the shoulders and muscles of the back
Tones the abdomen
Improves balance and posture
instructions: From a standing position, one leg is rooted and perpendicular to the earth while the other leg is raised, extended back and parallel to the earth
The head of the thighbone of the standing leg presses back towards the heel and is actively rooted into the earth
The arms and the extended leg lengthen in opposing directions with Bandhas engaged
The hips are squared and the tailbone presses firmly into the pelvis
The arms, torso, and extended raised leg should be positioned relatively parallel to the floor
The gaze is forward or down
pranayama_sync: Steady rhythmic breathing, gaze fixed
ayurvedic_rationale: Virabhadrasana Three extends the whole body into one horizontal line over a single leg, demanding strength and focus in equal measure. The commitment and precision are Pitta in character, the effort clears Kapha, and the intense concentration required leaves no room for Vata's mental scatter.

primary_benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves
Helps calm the nervous system
Improves flexibility in the posterior chain
Can reduce mild tension in the lower back when done gently
instructions: Stand in Mountain Pose with feet hip-width apart and knees soft.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hips, keeping the spine long.
If needed, bend the knees generously to bring the torso toward the thighs.
Hold the big toes with the index and middle fingers, or place hands on blocks/shins if needed.
Relax the neck and let the head hang without forcing the stretch.
With each inhale, lengthen the spine; with each exhale, deepen the fold slightly.
To exit, bend the knees and roll up slowly through the spine.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen the spine, and exhale to fold a little deeper while keeping the breath smooth and unforced.
ayurvedic_rationale: This forward fold is grounding and cooling, helping to pacify excess vata and pitta through gentle compression and inward attention. It is often used to quiet the mind and support a settling, restorative state after more active practice.

pranayama_sync: Exhale as you fold, breathe naturally in pose
ayurvedic_rationale: Uttanasana with a shoulder bind combines the cooling, inward quality of a forward fold with a strong opening across the front of the shoulders. The head-below-heart position calms Pitta and clears the Kapha mind. Keep the knees generously bent — length in the spine matters far more than straight legs.

primary_benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves
Relieves tension in the back body
Encourages spinal decompression
Promotes relaxation and introspection
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and soften the knees.
Fold forward from the hips, bringing the torso toward the thighs.
Slide the hands under the feet, palms up, with toes reaching toward the wrists if comfortable.
Keep the weight evenly distributed through the feet and avoid locking the knees.
Let the head and neck relax fully.
Use the breath to lengthen on the inhale and soften on the exhale.
To release, remove the hands from under the feet and slowly rise with a long spine.
pranayama_sync: Breathe steadily and allow each exhale to release tension in the hamstrings, back, and jaw.
ayurvedic_rationale: Padahastasana is a deeply grounding forward bend that can reduce excess vata by encouraging stillness and downward energy. Its mild compressive effect may also help settle pitta-driven agitation and mental overactivity.

primary_benefits: Lengthens the spine and teaches the flat-back position that protects the lumbar in every forward fold
Stretches the hamstrings without rounding the lower back
Strengthens the mid-back extensors and postural muscles
Builds the body awareness that makes deeper folds safe
instructions: From a standing forward fold, place the fingertips on the floor, on blocks, or on the shins.
Inhale and straighten the arms to lift the torso until the spine is parallel to the floor.
Draw the shoulder blades down the back and broaden the collarbones — do not let the shoulders creep toward the ears.
Lengthen the crown of the head forward and the tailbone back, creating one long line.
Keep a soft micro-bend in the knees so the length comes from the spine, not the hamstrings.
Gaze at the floor a few inches ahead to keep the neck in line with the spine.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lift and lengthen; exhale to fold deeper.
ayurvedic_rationale: Ardha Uttanasana is the alignment gateway of the Surya Namaskar sequence. Its calming forward orientation soothes Pitta while the spinal extension keeps Kapha from settling. For Vata, the half-fold is safer than the full fold, which can over-mobilise already loose joints.

primary_benefits: Stretches the hamstring, calf, and entire back line of the extended leg
Opens the hip and inner thigh of the bent leg
Calms the nervous system and quiets mental agitation
Compresses and stimulates the liver, kidneys, and digestive organs
instructions: Sit in Dandasana, then bend the right knee and draw the right heel toward the perineum, letting the knee open out to the side.
Sit on a folded blanket if the pelvis tilts backward — the fold must begin at the hips, not the waist.
Turn the torso to square it over the extended left leg before folding.
Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to hinge forward from the hip crease, reaching for the left foot or a strap around it.
Keep the left foot flexed and the left kneecap pointing straight up to protect the knee joint.
Hold, breathing into the back of the ribs. Rise on an inhale and change sides.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen the spine, exhale to fold. Let the exhale carry you deeper, never the effort.
ayurvedic_rationale: Janu Sirsasana is deeply Pitta-pacifying — the inward, downward fold cools the heat and drive of a Pitta mind. Classically used for digestive complaints, as the asymmetric compression massages the abdominal organs one side at a time. Vata types should sit elevated and keep the knee softly bent.

primary_benefits: Stretches the entire posterior chain — hamstrings, calves, and spine
Strongly activates the parasympathetic nervous system, easing anxiety and insomnia
Massages the abdominal organs and supports digestion and elimination
Relieves the compression of prolonged sitting through the lower back
instructions: Sit in Dandasana with the legs extended, feet flexed, and the thighs rooting down.
Sit on the front edge of a folded blanket so the pelvis can tip forward rather than tucking under.
Inhale, lift the arms overhead, and lengthen the whole spine.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hip creases, leading with the chest rather than the head.
Hold the shins, feet, or a strap looped around the soles — wherever you land with a long spine.
Soften the knees as much as needed. Let each exhale release you a little further without pulling.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to fold. Long, slow exhales deepen the calming effect.
ayurvedic_rationale: Paschimottanasana translates as the stretch of the west — the entire back body. It is the classical Pitta-cooling asana, drawing awareness inward and downward, and is prescribed across the Hatha texts for digestive fire regulation. Vata types must sit elevated with bent knees; the temptation to force this pose is exactly what aggravates Vata in the lumbar spine.

primary_benefits: Deeply opens the hamstrings of the front leg and the hip flexors and psoas of the back leg
Improves pelvic mobility and stride length
Releases the sciatic pathway when practised progressively
Builds patience and long-term consistency in the practice
instructions: Begin in a low lunge with the right foot forward and the left knee on the mat, placing a block under each hand.
Straighten the front leg progressively, sliding the right heel forward as the left thigh slides back.
Keep the hips square to the front — the left hip will want to swing open; draw it back and in.
Descend only as far as the hands can support with the pelvis level. Blocks or a bolster under the front thigh are not a compromise, they are the method.
Once at your depth, lengthen the spine and either stay upright or fold over the front leg.
Come out by bending the front knee and stepping back into a lunge. Repeat on the second side.
pranayama_sync: Long, slow exhales as you descend. Never hold the breath at your end range.
ayurvedic_rationale: Hanumanasana is named for the leap of Hanuman and demands sustained, patient effort rather than force. The deep hip opening releases Apana Vayu, the downward-moving air that governs elimination and where Vata most readily lodges. Never approach it cold — Vata aggravation in this pose means a strained hamstring insertion.

primary_benefits: Deeply opens the hips, groin, and adductors
Lengthens the entire spine and the muscles between the shoulder blades
Induces pratyahara — the withdrawal of the senses — through full forward enclosure
Profoundly calms an overactive nervous system
instructions: Sit with the legs wide and the knees bent, feet on the floor about a shoulder-width apart.
Fold forward and thread each arm underneath the corresponding knee, palms facing down.
Slide the arms out to the sides as the legs straighten gradually over the shoulders.
Lower the chest and chin toward the floor, letting the torso settle between the thighs.
Release the neck completely and let the weight of the legs do the work.
Stay for several slow breaths, then bend the knees and withdraw the arms to exit.
pranayama_sync: Slow, quiet breathing into the back of the ribs. Let the exhale lengthen naturally.
ayurvedic_rationale: Kurmasana takes its name from the tortoise withdrawing into its shell, and it is the archetypal pratyahara posture. Intensely Pitta-cooling and calming for an agitated mind. It requires open hips built over months — forcing it aggravates Vata in the sacroiliac joint and the groin.

primary_benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, adductors, and calves simultaneously
Decompresses the spine through gentle traction
Provides the calming effects of a mild inversion without load on the neck
Relieves tension headaches and mental fatigue
instructions: Step the feet 3 to 4 feet apart with the outer edges parallel and the toes pointing forward.
Place the hands on the hips, inhale, and lengthen the spine upward.
Exhale and hinge forward from the hip creases with a flat back, bringing the hands to the floor under the shoulders.
Walk the hands back until they are in line with the feet, elbows bending straight back.
Let the crown of the head release toward the floor; use a block under it if it does not reach.
Keep the weight slightly forward in the balls of the feet and the quadriceps engaged. Rise with a flat back on an inhale.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen, exhale to fold deeper. Rise on an inhale to avoid light-headedness.
ayurvedic_rationale: Prasarita Padottanasana cools and grounds. The head-below-heart position is calming for Pitta and clarifying for the Kapha mind, while the wide, stable base makes it one of the safest folds for Vata. Those with high blood pressure should keep the head above the heart and come up slowly.

primary_benefits: Strengthens shoulders, upper back, and core
Stretches hamstrings and calves
Prepares the body for forearm balance and other inversions
Builds shoulder stability without placing weight on the wrists
instructions: Start on hands and knees, then lower the forearms to the floor with elbows shoulder-width apart.
Interlace the fingers or keep the palms flat, and press the forearms down firmly.
Lift the knees and send the hips up and back, straightening the legs as much as comfortable.
Keep the head relaxed between the upper arms without collapsing into the shoulders.
Draw the ribs in and lengthen the spine while pressing the floor away through the forearms.
Hold with steady breathing, then lower the knees to the floor to rest.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen the spine and exhale to deepen the lift of the hips and engagement of the core.
ayurvedic_rationale: This pose creates heating, strengthening effort while opening the back body and calming excess kapha heaviness. Its downward-and-back shape can also help ground vata when practiced with steady breath and stable alignment.

primary_benefits: Builds significant shoulder, upper back, and core strength
Improves circulation and lymphatic return
Develops balance, spatial awareness, and mental steadiness
Strengthens the scapular stabilisers that protect the shoulder joint
instructions: Set up facing a wall in Dolphin Pose with the forearms parallel, shoulder-width apart, and the elbows directly under the shoulders.
Press the forearms and the outer wrists firmly down; the shoulders must stay stacked over the elbows throughout.
Walk the feet in toward the elbows until the hips are directly above the shoulders.
Lift one leg straight up, then hop lightly off the bottom foot with control — do not fling.
Once inverted, engage the core, lengthen the tailbone toward the heels, and avoid dumping into the lower back.
Come down one leg at a time, then rest in Child's Pose until the head-rush settles.
pranayama_sync: Steady Ujjayi. Never hold the breath while inverted — it spikes intracranial pressure.
ayurvedic_rationale: Pincha Mayurasana reverses the flow of Apana Vayu and stimulates the higher chakras. Its intensity generates Pitta and strongly reduces Kapha inertia. Vata types benefit from the grounding of pressing into the earth, but only with a wall and a genuinely conditioned shoulder girdle.

primary_benefits: Builds powerful shoulder, arm, and core strength
Improves balance, spatial awareness, and focus
Increases circulation and energizes the nervous system
Develops confidence and body control
instructions: Start in Downward-Facing Dog or a wall-supported setup with hands shoulder-width apart.
Place the hands firmly, spreading the fingers and pressing through the knuckles.
Walk the feet in and lift one leg high to create momentum with control.
Engage the core and kick lightly or float both legs up toward the wall or center line.
Stack wrists, elbows, shoulders, hips, and ankles as much as possible.
Keep the ribs from flaring, breathe steadily, and exit slowly with control.
pranayama_sync: Inhale to lengthen and prepare, then exhale to engage the core and lift, maintaining smooth nasal breathing throughout the inversion.
ayurvedic_rationale: As a strong inversion, this pose is highly stimulating and can reduce kapha heaviness while sharpening mental clarity. It may aggravate pitta due to its intensity and should be approached cautiously in states of heat, pressure, or depleted stability.

primary_benefits: Calms the brain
Stimulates the abdominal organs and the thyroid glands
Stretches the shoulders and spine
Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause
Reduces stress and fatigue
Therapeutic for backache, headache, infertility, insomnia,  and sinusitis
instructions: From a supine position, the upper back rests on the earth with the hips and legs revolved back over the torso above and beyond the head towards the earth
The torso is perpendicular to the earth
The legs are fully extended with no bend at the knees as the toes reach for the earth
The hands are either supporting the lower back or extended behind the back on the earth with extended elbows and fingers interlaced (as flexibility allows), opening the shoulders
The neck is straight
